text.p: Diversfield Perth-based industrial group Wesfarmers Ltd said on Tuesday that it has sold its half share in explosives manufacturing and marketing company Dyno Wesfarmers Ltd (DWL) to partner Dyno Industrier ASA of Norway.

The company said Dyno would pay A$50 million for the stake, along with Wesfarmers' interests in Dyno Wesfarmers (Hong Kong) Ltd and Thai Nitrate Co Ltd. Wesfarmers managing director Michael Chaney said the sale was due to be completed in early October and would realise a profit of about A$3.0 million.
Dyno has owned a 50 percent stake in DWL since 1988.

Chaney said the Wesfarmers investment had achieved its objective of helping the company build a strong market position in Asia and proceed with a A$70 million expansion of ammonium nitrate manufacturing facilities at Kwinana, Western Australia.
DWL would be renamed Dyno Nobel Asia Pacific Ltd after the sale, Chaney said.
